translations.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was with God in the beginning.
Everything came into being through him, and without him not one thing that came into being came into being.
In him was life, and that life is the light of humanity.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not grasp it.
There was a man sent from God whose name was John.
He came as a witness, to testify about the light, so that everyone might believe through him.
He was not the light, but came to testify about the light.
For there was the true light, which gives light to everyone who comes into the world.
He was in the world, and the world came into being through him, but the world did not know him.
He came to his own, and his own people did not receive him.
But to those who received him, who believe in his name, he gave the right to become children of God.
They were born not from blood, nor from the will of the flesh, nor from the will of a man, but from God.
The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.
John testified about him and cried out, saying, “This is the one of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has taken his place ahead of me, because he existed before me.’”
From his fullness we have all received, and grace in place of grace.
For the law was given through Moses, but truth and grace came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God. The only-begotten God, who is in the embrace of his Father, has made him known.
This is John's testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”
He confessed and did not deny it, but confessed, “I am not the Messiah.”
They asked him again, “What then? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” He said, “No.”
They said to him, “Who are you, then, so that we can give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say about yourself?”
He said, “I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, ‘Make the Lord’s way straight,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.”
Those who had been sent were from the Pharisees.
They asked him, “Why, then, do you baptize if you are not the Messiah, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?”
John answered them, “I baptize with water, but among you stands one whom you do not know.”
This is the one who comes after me and has taken precedence over me, whose sandal straps I am not worthy to untie.
These things happened in Bethany, across the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!”
“This is the one I spoke about when I said, ‘After me comes a man who has taken precedence over me, because he existed before me.’
I did not know him, but I came baptizing with water so that he might be made known to Israel.”
John testified, saying, “I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it remained on him.
I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water told me, ‘The one on whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.’
I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God.”
The next day John was standing with two of his disciples.
He looked at Jesus as he walked by and said, “Look, the Lamb of God!”
Both his disciples heard him say this and followed Jesus.
Jesus turned and saw them following him. He said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to him, “Our teacher, where are you staying?”
He said to them, “Come and see.” So they came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
One of those who heard John and followed Jesus was Andrew, Simon’s brother.
He first found his brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Messiah.”
He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon, the son of Jonah. You will be called Cephas.”
The next day Jesus wanted to leave for Galilee. He found Philip and said to him, “Follow me.”
Philip was from Bethsaida, the town of Andrew and Simon.
Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found the one whom Moses wrote about in the Law and in the Prophets: Jesus, the son of Joseph, from Nazareth.”
Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said about him, “Look, a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit!”
Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?” Jesus said to him, “Before Philip called you, I saw you when you were under the fig tree.”
Nathanael answered him, “My teacher, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”
Jesus said to him, “Do you believe because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.”
He said to him, “Truly, truly, I tell you all, from now on you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending toward the Son of Man.”
On the third day there was a wedding feast in Cana, a town in Galilee, and Jesus’ mother was there.
Jesus himself and his disciples were also invited to the wedding feast.
The wine had run out, and Jesus’ mother said to him, “They have no wine.”
Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does this have to do with you and me? My hour has not yet come.”
His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
There were six stone jars there, set aside for the Jewish purification rites, each holding two or three measures.
Jesus said to them, “Fill the jars with water.” And they filled them to the brim.
He said to them, “Now draw some out and take it to the master of the banquet.” And they took it.

When the master of the banquet tasted the water that had become wine, he did not know where it had come from. But the servants knew, because they had filled the jars with water. The master of the banquet called the bridegroom
and said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when people have become drunk, then the inferior wine. But you have kept the good wine until now.”
This was the first sign Jesus performed in Cana of Galilee. He revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
After this he went down to Capernaum with his mother, his brothers, and his disciples. They stayed there a few days.
The Jewish Passover was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In the temple he found people selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers sitting there.
He made himself a whip from rope and drove them all out of the temple—the sheep, the cattle, and the money changers. He scattered their money and overturned their tables.
He said to those selling doves, “Take these away from here! Do not make my Father’s house a marketplace.”
His disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house has consumed me.”
The Jews responded by saying to him, “What sign can you show us to justify doing these things?”
Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
The Jews said to him, “It took forty-six years to build this temple, and you will raise it up in three days?”
But he was speaking about the temple of his body.
When he rose from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scriptures and the word Jesus had spoken.
While Jesus was in Jerusalem at the Passover festival, many believed in him because they saw the signs he was performing.
But Jesus himself did not entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone.
He did not need anyone to testify to him about any human being, for he himself knew what was in a human being.
There was a man there from among the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews.
He came to Jesus at night and said to him, “Rabbi, we know that you have been sent from God as a teacher, for no one can perform these signs you perform unless God is with him.”
Jesus answered him, “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless someone is born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”
Nicodemus said to him, “How can an old man be born? Can he enter his mother’s womb a second time and be born?”
Jesus answered him, “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless someone is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.”
What is born of flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
Do not be amazed that I told you, ‘You must be born again.’
The wind blows where it wishes, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit.
Nicodemus answered him, ‘How can these things happen?’
Jesus answered him, ‘You are Israel’s teacher, and you do not understand these things?
Truly, truly, I tell you: we speak about what we know and testify to what we have seen, but you do not accept our testimony.
If I have told you about earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe me if I tell you about heavenly things?
No one has gone up to heaven except the one who came down from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven.
Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man is to be lifted up,
so that everyone who believes in him will not perish but will have eternal life.
For God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him will not perish but will have eternal life.
For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through him.
Whoever believes in him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe is already condemned, because he has not believed in the name of God’s only Son.
This is the judgment: light came into the world, but people loved darkness more than light, because their deeds were evil.
For everyone who does hateful things hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his deeds will not be exposed.
But whoever practices the truth comes to the light, so that his deeds may be known to have been done in God.’
After these things, Jesus and his disciples came into the land of Judea. He stayed there with them and baptized.
John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there. People were coming and being baptized.
For John had not yet been put in prison.
Now a dispute arose between one of John’s disciples and a Jew about purification.
They came to John and said to him, ‘Our teacher, the man who was with you across the Jordan, about whom you testified—look, he too is baptizing, and many people are coming to him.’
John answered them, ‘A person cannot receive anything by his own will unless it has been given to him from heaven.
You yourselves are my witnesses that I said, ‘I am not the Messiah, but I have been sent ahead of him.’
The one who has the bride is the bridegroom. But the bridegroom’s friend, who stands and listens to him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom’s voice. So this joy of mine is now complete.
He must increase, and I must decrease.
For the one who came from above is above all. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks of earthly things. The one who came from heaven is above all.
He testifies to what he has seen and heard, but no one accepts his testimony.
But whoever has accepted his testimony has confirmed that God is truthful.
For the one whom God has sent speaks God's words, because God does not give the Spirit in a limited measure.
The Father loves the Son and has put everything into his hands.
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. But whoever does not obey the Son will not see life; instead, God's wrath will remain on him.
Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard that he was making and baptizing more disciples than John.
Yet it was not Jesus himself who was baptizing, but his disciples.
He left Judea and went back to Galilee.
He had to pass through Samaritan territory.
He came to a Samaritan town called Sychar, near the village that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
Jacob's spring of water was there. Jesus was tired from the strain of the journey, so he sat down by the spring. It was the sixth hour.
A woman from Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, "Give me some water to drink."
For his disciples had gone into the town to buy food for themselves.
The Samaritan woman said to him, "How can you, a Jew, ask me, a Samaritan woman, for a drink?" For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.
Jesus answered her, "If you knew God's gift and who it is who said to you, 'Give me a drink,' you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water."
The woman said to him, "Sir, you have no bucket, and the well is deep. Where will you get living water?
Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well and drank from it himself, along with his sons and his flocks?"
Jesus answered her, "Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.
But whoever drinks the water that I will give him will never be thirsty. Instead, the water that I give him will become within him a spring of water welling up to eternal life."
The woman said to him, "Sir, give me some of this water so that I will no longer be thirsty or keep coming here to draw water."
Jesus said to her, "Go, call your husband, and come here."
She said to him, "I have no husband." Jesus said to her, "You are right to say, 'I have no husband.'
For you have had five husbands, and the man you have now is not your husband. What you have said is true."
The woman said to him, "Sir, I see that you are a prophet.
Our ancestors worshiped on this mountain, but you say that Jerusalem is the place where people must worship."
Jesus said to her, "Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
You worship what you do not know, but we worship what we know, because salvation comes from the Jews.
But the time is coming, and is now here, when true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth. For the Father seeks worshipers like these.
For God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and in truth.
The woman said to him, “I know that the Messiah is coming. When he comes, he will teach us everything.”
Jesus said to her, “I am he, the one speaking with you.”
While he was speaking, his disciples came and were astonished that he was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said, “What are you seeking?” or “Why are you speaking with her?”
The woman left her water jar, went into the town, and said to the people:
Come and see a man who told me everything I have done. Could he be the Messiah?
The people went out of the town and were coming to him.
Meanwhile, his disciples urged him, saying, “Our teacher, eat.”
But he said to them, “I have food to eat that you do not know about.”
The disciples said to one another, “Has someone brought him something to eat?”
Jesus said to them, “My food is to do the will of the one who sent me and to complete his work.
Do you not say, ‘The harvest comes after four months’? Look, I tell you, lift up your eyes and see the fields: they are already white and ready for harvest.
The one who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.
For in this the saying holds true: ‘One sows and another reaps.’
I sent you to reap what you had not worked for. Others did the hard work, and you have entered into their labor.”
Many Samaritans from that town believed in him because of the woman's words, as she testified, “He told me everything I have done.”
When those Samaritans came to him, they asked him to stay with them, and he stayed with them for two days.
And many believed in him because of his words.
They said to the woman, “We no longer believe in him because of your words, for we have heard for ourselves and know that he truly is the Messiah, the Savior of the world.”
After two days, Jesus left there and went to Galilee.
For Jesus himself testified that a prophet is not honored in his own town.
When he came to Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, having seen all the signs he had performed in Jerusalem at the festival, for they too had gone to the festival.
Jesus came again to Cana in Galilee, where he had made the water into wine. There was a royal official in Capernaum whose son was sick.
When this man heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son, for he was close to death.
Jesus said to him, “Unless you all see signs and wonders, you will not believe.”
The royal official said to him, “Sir, come down before the boy dies.”
Jesus said to him, “Go; your son is alive.” The man believed the word Jesus had spoken to him and went.
While he was going down, his servants met him and brought him good news, saying, “Your son is alive.”
He asked them at what time he had recovered. They told him, “Yesterday, at the seventh hour, the fever left him.”
The father realized that it was at the very hour when Jesus had told him, “Your son is alive.” And he and his entire household believed.
This was the second sign Jesus performed when he came again from Judea to Galilee.
After these things, there was a Jewish festival, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
There was a place in Jerusalem with a bathing pool, called Bethesda in Hebrew. It had five colonnades.
In these lay a large crowd of sick people, blind people, people who were lame, and people with withered limbs. They were waiting for the water to move.
For an angel would come down into the pool from time to time and stir the water. Whoever went down first after the water was stirred would be healed of whatever illness he had.
There was a man there who had been ill for thirty-eight years.
Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had been that way for a long time. He said to him, “Do you want to get well?”
The sick man answered, “Yes, sir. But I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am coming, someone else goes down ahead of me.”
Jesus said to him, “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.”
Immediately the man was healed. He got up, picked up his mat, and walked. That day was the Sabbath.
The Jews said to the man who had been healed, “It is the Sabbath. You are not allowed to carry your mat.”
But he answered them, “The one who made me well told me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’”
They asked him, “Who is this man who told you, ‘Pick up your mat and walk’?”
But the man who had been healed did not know who he was, for Jesus had concealed himself in the large crowd that was in that place.
Some time later, Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, “Look, you are well. Do not sin again, or something worse than before may happen to you.”
The man went and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
Because of this, the Jews were persecuting Jesus and seeking to kill him, because he was doing these things on the Sabbath.
But Jesus said to them, “My Father is working even now, and I too am working.”
Because of this, the Jews sought all the more to kill him, not only because he was breaking the Sabbath, but also because he said that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.
Jesus answered them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing of his own will, but only what he sees the Father doing. For whatever the Father does, the Son also does in the same way.
For the Father loves his Son and shows him everything he does. And he will show him greater works than these, so that you will marvel.
For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so the Son also gives life to those he wishes.
For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son,
so that everyone may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.
Truly, truly, I tell you: whoever hears my word and believes the one who sent me has eternal life and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death to life.
Truly, truly, I tell you: the hour is coming, and is already here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
For just as the Father has life in himself, so he has also granted the Son to have life in himself.
And he also gave him authority to carry out judgment.
But because he is the Son of Man, do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming when all those in the tombs will hear his voice
and come out: those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
I can do nothing of my own will. Rather, I judge as I hear, and my judgment is just, because I do not seek my own will, but the will of the one who sent me.
If I testify about myself, my testimony is not true.
There is another who testifies about me, and I know that the testimony he gives about me is true.
You sent to John, and he testified to the truth.
But I do not receive testimony from a human being. Rather, I say these things so that you may live.
He was a burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light.
But I have testimony greater than John's. For the works that my Father gave me to complete—the very works I do—testify about me that the Father sent me.
And the Father who sent me himself testifies about me. You have never heard his voice or seen his form.
And his word does not remain in you, because you do not believe in the one he sent.
Search the Scriptures, in which you think you have eternal life. They testify about me.
And you are unwilling to come to me so that you may have eternal life.
I do not receive praise from people.
But I know you: you do not have the love of God in you.
I have come in my Father's name, and you do not accept me. If another comes in his own name, you will accept him.
How can you believe, when you accept praise from one another but do not seek the praise that comes from the one God?
Do you think that I accuse you before the Father? There is someone who accuses you: Moses, in whom you have placed your hope.
For if you believed Moses, you would also believe me, because Moses wrote about me.
But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?
After these things, Jesus went to the other side of the Sea of Galilee, the Sea of Tiberias.
Large crowds followed him because they saw the signs he was performing on the sick.
Jesus went up the mountain and sat there with his disciples.
Now the Jewish Passover festival was near.
Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming toward him. He said to Philip, “Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?”
He said this to test him, for he himself knew what he was going to do.
Philip said to him, “Two hundred denarii worth of bread would not be enough for them, even if each one took just a little.”
One of his disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, said to him:
“There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish. But what are these for so many people?”
Jesus said to them, “Have all the people sit down.” There was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down, numbering five thousand.
Jesus took the bread, blessed it, and distributed it to those who were seated. He did the same with the fish, giving them as much as they wanted.
When they had eaten their fill, he said to his disciples, “Gather up the leftover pieces so that nothing is lost.”
They gathered them up and filled twelve baskets with pieces left over by those who had eaten from the five barley loaves.
When the people saw the sign Jesus had performed, they said, “This truly is the prophet who is coming into the world.”
But Jesus knew that they were about to come and seize him to make him king, so he withdrew to the mountain by himself.
When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea.
They got into a boat and set out across the sea toward Capernaum. It had grown dark, and Jesus had not come to them.
The sea was rising against them because a strong wind was blowing.
When they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea. As he approached their boat, they became afraid.
But Jesus said to them, “It is I. Do not be afraid.”
They wanted to take him into the boat, and immediately the boat reached the land where they were going.

The next day, the crowd standing on the other side of the sea saw that there had been no other boat there except the one the disciples had boarded, and that Jesus had not entered the boat with his disciples.
But other boats had come from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread after Jesus had blessed it.
When the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor his disciples were there, they got into these boats and came to Capernaum, looking for Jesus.
When they found him on the other side of the sea, they said to him, “Rabbi, when did you come here?”
Jesus answered them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, you are looking for me not because you saw signs, but because you ate the bread and had your fill.
Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that lasts for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For God the Father has set his seal on him.”
They said to him, “What must we do to carry out the works of God?”
Jesus answered them, “This is the work of God: that you believe in the one he sent.”
They said to him, “What sign will you perform so that we may see it and believe in you? What will you do?
Our ancestors ate manna in the wilderness, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”
Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it was not Moses who gave you bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.”
“For the bread of God is the one who came down from heaven and gives life to the world.”
They said to him, “Our Lord, always give us this bread.”
Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not go hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.”
“But I told you that you have seen me and do not believe.”
“Everyone my Father has given me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will not turn away.”
“For I came down from heaven not to do my own will, but to do the will of the one who sent me.”
“Now this is the will of the one who sent me: that I should lose none of those he has given me, but raise them up on the last day.”
“For this is my Father’s will: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, and I will raise them up on the last day.”
But the Jews were grumbling about him because he said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”
They were saying, “Isn't this Jesus, Joseph's son, whose father and mother we know? How can he say, ‘I came down from heaven’?”
Jesus answered them, “Do not grumble among yourselves.”
“No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws them, and I will raise them up on the last day.”
“For it is written in the prophet, ‘They will all be taught by God.’ So everyone who hears from the Father and learns from him comes to me.”
Not that anyone has seen the Father, except the one who is from God; he has seen the Father.
“Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in me has eternal life.”
“I am the bread of life.”
“Your ancestors ate manna in the wilderness and died.”
“But this is the bread that came down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.”
“I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, they will live forever. And the bread that I will give is my body, which I give for the life of the world.”
Then the Jews were arguing with one another, saying, “How can this man give us his body to eat?”
Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the body of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in yourselves.”
“But whoever eats of my body and drinks of my blood has eternal life, and I will raise them up on the last day.”
“For my body is truly food, and my blood is truly drink.”
“Whoever eats my body and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in them.”
“Just as the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so whoever eats me will also live because of me.”
“This is the bread that came down from heaven, not like the manna your ancestors ate and died. Whoever eats this bread will live forever.”
He said these things in the synagogue while teaching in Capernaum.
Many of his disciples who heard this said, “This statement is hard. Who can listen to it?”
But Jesus knew within himself that his disciples were grumbling about this, and he said to them, “Does this make you stumble?
Then what if you see the Son of Man ascending to where he was before?
It is the Spirit who gives life; the body is of no benefit at all. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and life.
But there are some among you who do not believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who those who did not believe were, and who would betray him.
And he said to them, “This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless it is granted to them by my Father.”
Because of this statement, many of his disciples turned back and no longer walked with him.
Jesus said to his twelve, “Do you also want to leave?”
Simon Peter answered, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.”
And we have believed and have come to know that you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.
Jesus said to them, “Did I not choose you twelve? Yet one of you is a devil.”
He was speaking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, for he was going to betray him, though he was one of the twelve.
After these things, Jesus traveled around Galilee. He did not want to travel around Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill him.
Now the Jewish Festival of Shelters was near.
Jesus’ brothers said to him, “Leave here and go to Judea, so that your disciples may see the works you are doing.
For no one does anything in secret while wanting to be publicly known. If you do these things, show yourself to the world.”
For not even his brothers believed in him, Jesus.
Jesus said to them, “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.
The world cannot hate you, but it hates me because I testify against it that its deeds are evil.
You go up to this festival. I am not going up to this festival now, because my time has not yet fully come.”
He said these things and remained in Galilee.
But after his brothers had gone up to the festival, he too went up, not openly, but as though in secret.
The Jews were looking for him at the festival and were saying, “Where is he?”
There was much murmuring about him among the crowd. Some were saying, “He is good,” while others were saying, “No, he leads the people astray.”
But no one spoke openly about him for fear of the Jews.
When the festival was halfway through, Jesus went up to the temple and began teaching.
The Jews were amazed and said, “How does this man know the Scriptures when he has not studied?”
Jesus answered, “My teaching is not mine, but belongs to the one who sent me.”
“Anyone who wants to do his will will understand whether my teaching is from God or whether I speak on my own initiative.”
“Anyone who speaks from his own thinking seeks glory for himself. But anyone who seeks the glory of the one who sent him is truthful, and there is no wrongdoing in his heart.”
“Did not Moses give you the law? Yet none of you keeps the law.”
“Why are you trying to kill me?” The crowd answered, “You have a demon! Who is trying to kill you?”
Jesus answered them, “I did one deed, and you are all amazed.”
“For this reason Moses gave you circumcision—not that it originated with Moses, but with the ancestors—and you circumcise a person on the Sabbath.”
“If a person is circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses will not be broken, are you grumbling against me because I made a person completely well on the Sabbath?”
“Do not judge with partiality, but judge fairly.”
Some people from Jerusalem were saying, “Is this not the man they are trying to kill?”
“Look, he is speaking openly, and they say nothing to him. Could our elders have recognized that this really is the Messiah?”
“But we know where this man comes from. When the Messiah comes, no one will know where he comes from.”

Then Jesus raised his voice as he taught in the temple and said, “You know me, and you know where I come from. Yet I have not come on my own initiative. The one who sent me is true, and you do not know him.”
“But I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.”
They tried to seize him, but no one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come.
But many in the crowd believed in him and said, “When the Messiah comes, will he perform more signs than this man does?”
The Pharisees heard the crowds saying these things about him, and they and the chief priests sent guards to seize him.
Jesus said, “I am with you a little while longer, and then I am going to the one who sent me.”
“You will look for me and will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come.”
The Jews said among themselves, “Where is this man going that we will not find him? Is he going to the lands of the nations to teach the pagans?”
“What does this statement of his mean: ‘You will look for me and will not find me,’ and ‘Where I am, you cannot come’?”
On the great day, the last day of the festival, Jesus stood and cried out, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink.”
“Whoever believes in me, as the Scriptures have said, rivers of living water will flow from within him.”
He said this about the Spirit, whom those who believed in him were going to receive. For the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
Many in the crowds who heard his words said, “This truly is the Prophet.”
Others said, “This is the Messiah.” Others said, “Surely the Messiah does not come from Galilee?
Does not Scripture say that the Messiah comes from David’s descendants and from Bethlehem, David’s village?”
So there was a division among the crowds because of him.
Some of them wanted to arrest him, but no one laid hands on him.
Those guards came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and the priests said to them, “Why did you not bring him?”
The guards said to them, “No one has ever spoken the way this man speaks.”
The Pharisees said to them, “Have you also been led astray?
Has any of the rulers or Pharisees believed in him?
But this crowd, which does not know the law—they are cursed!”
Nicodemus, one of them, who had come to Jesus at night, said to them,
“Does our law condemn a person without first hearing from him and finding out what he has done?”
They answered him, “Are you also from Galilee? Search and see that no prophet arises from Galilee.”
Then everyone went to his own home.
But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
In the morning he came to the temple again, and all the people were coming to him. He sat down and taught them.
The scribes and Pharisees brought a woman who had been caught in adultery. They made her stand in the middle,
and said to him, “Teacher, this woman was caught openly in the very act of adultery.
In the law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. What, then, do you say?”
They said this to test him, so that they would have grounds to accuse him. But Jesus bent down and wrote on the ground.
When they kept questioning him, he straightened up and said to them, “Let whichever of you is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her.”
He bent down again and wrote on the ground.
When they heard this, they went out one by one, beginning with the oldest, and the woman was left alone, standing in the middle.
Jesus straightened up and said to the woman, “Where are they? Has no one condemned you?”
She said, “No one, Lord.” Then Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go, and from now on do not sin again.”
Jesus spoke with them again and said, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life.”
The Pharisees said to him, “You are testifying about yourself. Your testimony is not true.”
Jesus answered them, “Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I came from or where I am going.”
“You judge by human standards. I judge no one.”
“But even if I judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I am with my Father who sent me.”
“It is also written in your law that the testimony of two men is true.”
“I am the one who testifies about myself, and my Father who sent me testifies about me.”
They said to him, “Where is your Father?” Jesus answered them, “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would also know my Father.”
He spoke these words in the treasury while teaching in the temple, and no one arrested him, because his hour had not yet come.
Jesus said to them again, “I am going away. You will look for me, and you will die in your sins. Where I am going, you cannot come.”
The Jews said, “Is he going to kill himself, since he says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”
He said to them, “You are from below, and I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world.”
“I told you that you will die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sins.”
The Jews said, “Who are you?” Jesus said to them, “Even though I have begun to speak with you,”
“I have much to say about you and to judge. But the one who sent me is truthful, and what I heard from him is what I speak in the world.”
They did not understand that he was speaking to them about the Father.
Jesus said to them again, “When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am, and that I do nothing of my own will, but speak just as my Father taught me.”
“The one who sent me is with me. My Father has not left me alone, because I always do what pleases him.”
As he was saying these things, many believed in him.
Jesus said to those Jews who believed in him, “If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples.”
“You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”
They said to him, “We are Abraham’s descendants, and we have never served anyone as slaves. How can you say, ‘You will become free’?”
Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin.”
A slave does not remain in the house forever, but the son remains forever.
So if the Son sets you free, you will truly be free.
I know that you are Abraham’s descendants. Yet you are trying to kill me because you cannot bear my word.
I speak about what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have seen with your father.
They answered him, “Our father is Abraham.” Jesus said to them, “If you were Abraham’s children, you would do what Abraham did.”
But now you are seeking to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.
“But you do what your father does.” They said to him, “We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father: God.”
Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came forth from God and have come here. I did not come of my own will, but he sent me.”
“Why do you not understand what I say? Because you cannot listen to my word.”

“You are from your father, the devil, and you want to carry out your father’s desire. He has been a murderer from the beginning and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks falsehood, he speaks from what is his own, because he is a liar, and so is his father.”
“But because I speak the truth, you do not believe me.”
“Which of you can convict me of sin? And if I speak the truth, why do you not believe me?”
“Whoever is from God listens to God’s words. This is why you do not listen: because you are not from God.”
The Jews answered him, “Are we not right to say that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?”
Jesus said to them, “I do not have a demon. Rather, I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.”
“I do not seek my own glory. There is one who seeks it and judges.”
“Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever keeps my word will never see death.”
The Jews said to him, “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet you say, ‘Whoever keeps my word will never taste death.’”
“Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died, and than the prophets, who died? Who do you make yourself out to be?”
Jesus said to them, “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, the one of whom you say, ‘He is our God.’”
“You have not known him, but I know him. If I say that I do not know him, I will be a liar like you. But I know him and keep his word.”
“Your father Abraham longed to see my day. He saw it and rejoiced.”
The Jews said to him, “You are not yet fifty years old, and you have seen Abraham?”
Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, before Abraham came into being, I am.”
They picked up stones to stone him, but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple. He passed through their midst and went away.
As he passed by, he saw a man who had been blind from his mother’s womb.
His disciples asked him, “Our teacher, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”
Jesus said to them, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that God’s works might be revealed in him.
I must do the works of the one who sent me while it is day. Night is coming, when no one can work.
As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
After saying these things, he spat on the ground, made mud with his saliva, and spread it on the blind man’s eyes.
He said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam.” He went and washed and came back able to see.
His neighbors and those who had previously seen him begging were saying, “Isn't this the man who used to sit and beg?”
Some said, “It is he.” Others said, “No, he only looks like him.” But he himself said, “I am the man.”
They said to him, “How were your eyes opened?”
He answered them, “A man named Jesus made mud, spread it on my eyes, and said to me, ‘Go, wash in the water of Siloam.’ So I went and washed, and I could see.”
They said to him, “Where is he?” He said to them, “I do not know.”
They brought the man who had formerly been blind to the Pharisees.
Now it was the Sabbath when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.
The Pharisees also asked him how he had come to see. He said to them, “He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and I could see.”
Some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath.” But others said, “How can a sinful man perform these signs?” And there was a division among them.
They said again to the blind man, “What do you say about him, since he opened your eyes?” He said to them, “I say that he is a prophet.”
But the Jews did not believe that he had been blind and had come to see until they called the parents of the man who had come to see.
They asked them, “Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? How, then, can he see now?”
His parents answered, “We know that this is our son and that he was born blind.
But how he can see now, or who opened his eyes, we do not know. He is old enough; ask him. He will speak for himself.”
His parents said these things because they were afraid of the Jews, for the Jews had already decided that if anyone acknowledged him as the Messiah, they would expel that person from the synagogue.
That is why his parents said, “He is old enough; ask him.”
They called the man who had been blind a second time and said to him, “Give glory to God, for we know that this man is a sinner.”
He answered them, “Whether he is a sinner, I do not know. But one thing I do know: I was blind, and now, look, I can see!”
They said to him again, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”
He said to them, “I told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you too want to become his disciples?”
But they insulted him and said to him, "You are that man's disciple, but we are disciples of Moses."
"We know that God spoke with Moses, but as for this man, we do not know where he comes from."
The man answered them, "This is what is astonishing: you do not know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes!"
"Now we know that God does not listen to the voice of sinners. Rather, he listens to anyone who fears him and does his will."
"Never since the world began has anyone heard of someone opening the eyes of a person born blind."
"If this man were not from God, he could not have done this."
They answered him, "You were born entirely in sins, and you are teaching us?" And they threw him out.
Jesus heard that they had thrown him out. He found him and said to him, "Do you believe in the Son of God?"
The man who had been healed answered, "Who is he, my lord, so that I may believe in him?"
Jesus said to him, "You have seen him, and he is the one speaking with you."
He said, "I believe, Lord," and fell down and worshiped him.
Jesus said, "I came to judge this world, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind."
Some of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things and said to him, "Are we blind too?"
Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would have no sin. But now you say, 'We see.' Because of this, your sin remains."
"Truly, truly, I tell you, anyone who does not enter the sheepfold through the gate, but climbs in somewhere else, is a thief and a robber."
"But the one who enters through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep."
"The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his sheep by their names and leads them out."
"When he has brought his flock out, he goes ahead of it, and his own sheep follow him because they know his voice."
"But the sheep will not follow a stranger. Instead, they run away from him because they do not know the stranger's voice."
Jesus told them this illustration, but they did not understand what he was saying to them.
So Jesus said to them again, "Truly, truly, I tell you, I am the gate for the sheep."
"All those who came are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them."
"I am the gate. If anyone enters through me, he will live. He will go in and out and find pasture."
"The thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I came so that they may have life and have more than enough."
"I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep."
But the hired worker, who is not the shepherd and does not own the sheep, leaves the flock and runs away when he sees the wolf coming. Then the wolf comes, snatches the sheep, and scatters the flock.
The hired worker runs away because he is a hired worker and does not care about the flock.
I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and my own know me.
Just as my Father knows me, I also know my Father. And I lay down my life for the flock.
I also have other sheep that are not from this fold. I must bring them too, and they will hear my voice. The whole flock will be one, with one shepherd.
This is why my Father loves me: because I lay down my life so that I may take it up again.
No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own will. For I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again. I received this command from my Father.
There was again a division among the Jews because of these words.
Many of them were saying, “He has a demon and is raving mad. Why do you listen to him?”
But others were saying, “These are not the words of someone possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”
Then the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem, and it was winter.
Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon’s colonnade.
The Jews surrounded him and said to him, “How long will you keep us in suspense? If you are the Messiah, tell us plainly.”
Jesus answered them, “I told you, and you do not believe. The works I do in my Father’s name testify about me.
But you do not believe because you are not among my sheep, as I told you.
My sheep hear my voice. I know them, and they follow me.
I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one will snatch them from my hands.
For my Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all, and no one can snatch them from my Father’s hand.
I and my Father are one.”
The Jews again picked up stones to stone him.
Jesus said to them, “I have shown you many good works from my Father. For which of them are you stoning me?”
The Jews said to him, “We are not stoning you for good works, but because you blaspheme. Though you are a human being, you make yourself God.”
Jesus said to them, “Is it not written in your law, ‘I said, you are gods’?
If he called them gods because the word of God came to them—and Scripture cannot be set aside—
do you say to the one whom the Father consecrated and sent into the world, ‘You are blaspheming,’ because I told you, ‘I am the Son of God’?
If I do not do my Father’s works, do not believe me.
But if I do them, even if you do not believe me, believe the works, so that you may know and believe that my Father is in me and I am in my Father.
Again they tried to seize him, but he escaped from their hands.
He went across the Jordan to the place where John had previously been baptizing, and he stayed there.
Many people came to him and said, “John did not perform even one sign, but everything John said about this man is true.”
And many believed in him.
Now a man was sick, Lazarus from the village of Bethany, the brother of Mary and Martha.
This Mary was the one who anointed Jesus’ feet with perfume and wiped them with her hair. It was her brother Lazarus who was sick.
His two sisters sent word to Jesus, saying, “Our Lord, look, the one you love is sick.”
But Jesus said, “This sickness is not for death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”
Now Jesus loved Martha, Mary, and Lazarus.
When he heard that Lazarus was sick, he stayed where he was for two days.
After that he said to his disciples, “Come, let us go to Judea again.”
His disciples said to him, “Our teacher, the Jews were just trying to stone you, and you are going there again?”
Jesus said to them, “Are there not twelve hours in the day? If someone walks during the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
But if someone walks at night, he stumbles, because there is no light in him.”
Jesus said these things, and afterward he told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going to wake him.”
His disciples said to him, “Our Lord, if he is asleep, he will recover.”
Jesus was speaking about his death, but they thought he was speaking about resting in sleep.
Then Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus has died.
And for your sake I am glad that I was not there, so that you may believe. But go there.”
Thomas, who is called the Twin, said to his fellow disciples, “Let us go too, so that we may die with him.”
Jesus came to Bethany and found that Lazarus had been in the tomb for four days.
Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
Many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to comfort them over their brother.
When Martha heard that Jesus had come, she went out to meet him, while Mary remained seated in the house.
Martha said to Jesus, “My Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
But even now I know that whatever you ask of God, he will give you.”
Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise.”
Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.”
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me will live, even if he dies.”
“And everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
She said to him, “Yes, Lord. I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, who is coming into the world.”
After saying this, she went and called her sister Mary privately, saying to her, “Our Teacher has come and is calling for you.”
When Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to him.
Jesus had not yet entered the village but was still at the place where Martha had met him.
When the Jews who were with her in the house comforting her saw Mary get up quickly and leave, they followed her, thinking that she was going to the tomb to weep.
When Mary came to where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said to him, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”
When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, he became deeply agitated in spirit and troubled himself.
He said, “Where have you laid him?” They said to him, “Lord, come and see.”
Jesus shed tears.
The Jews said, “See how much he loved him!”
But some of them said, “Could not this man, who opened the blind man’s eyes, have kept this man from dying too?”
Jesus, deeply agitated within himself, came to the tomb. The tomb was a cave, and a stone had been placed over its entrance.
Jesus said, “Take away this stone.” Martha, the dead man’s sister, said to him, “Lord, he already smells of decay, for he has been dead four days.”
Jesus said to her, “Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?”
They took away the stone. Jesus lifted his eyes upward and said, “Father, I thank you that you have heard me.”
“I know that you always hear me, but I am saying these things for the sake of this crowd standing here, so that they may believe that you sent me.”
After saying this, he cried out in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”
The dead man came out, with his hands and feet bound in strips of cloth and his face wrapped in a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Unbind him and let him go.”
Many of the Jews who had come to Mary believed in him when they saw what Jesus had done.
But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
The chief priests and the Pharisees gathered together and said, “What are we to do? This man is performing many signs.”
“If we let him go on like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away our land and our people.”
One of them, named Caiaphas, was high priest that year. He said to them, “You know nothing at all.”
And you do not consider that it is better for us that one man should die for the people than that the whole people should perish.
He did not say this on his own initiative. Rather, because he was high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was going to die for the people,
and not only for the people, but also to gather God's scattered children into one.
From that day on, they planned to kill him.
Jesus therefore no longer went about openly among the Jews. Instead, he left there for the region near the wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, and stayed there with his disciples.
The Jewish Passover was near, and many people went up from the villages to Jerusalem before the festival to purify themselves.
They were looking for Jesus and saying to one another in the temple, “What do you think? Will he not come to the festival?”
The chief priests and the Pharisees had ordered that if anyone knew where he was, they should report it to them so that they could arrest him.
Six days before Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus himself had raised from the dead.
They prepared a supper for him there. Martha was serving, and Lazarus was one of those reclining at the table with him.
Mary took a jar of very expensive perfume made from the finest nard, anointed Jesus' feet, and wiped his feet with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples, who was going to betray him, said,
“Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor?”
He said this not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. He had charge of the money box and carried what was put into it.
But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. She has kept it for the day of my burial.
For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.”
Large crowds of Jews heard that Jesus was there and came, not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.
The chief priests planned to kill Lazarus too,
because many of the Jews were going away and believing in Jesus because of him.
The next day, when the large crowd that was coming to the festival heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
they took palm branches and went out to meet him, shouting, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!”
Jesus found a donkey and sat on it, as it is written:
“Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion. Look, your king is coming to you, riding on a colt, the foal of a donkey.”

His disciples did not understand these things at that time. But when Jesus was glorified, his disciples remembered that these things had been written about him and that they had done these things for him.
The crowd that had been with him testified that he had called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead.
This was why large crowds went out to meet him: they had heard that he had performed this sign.
But the Pharisees were saying to one another, “You see that you are accomplishing nothing. Look, the whole world has gone after him!”
There were also some Gentiles among those who had gone up to worship at the festival.
They approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and asked him, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
Philip went and told Andrew, and Andrew and Philip told Jesus.
Jesus answered them, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it remains alone. But if it dies, it produces much fruit.
Whoever loves his life will lose it, and whoever hates his life in this world will preserve it for eternal life.
If anyone serves me, let him follow me. Where I am, my servant will also be. The Father will honor whoever serves me.
Now my soul is troubled. What shall I say? ‘My Father, save me from this hour’? But it was for this that I came to this hour.
Father, glorify your name.” Then a voice was heard from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”
The crowd standing there heard it and said, “It was thunder.” But others said, “An angel spoke to him.”
Jesus answered them, “This voice came not for my sake, but for yours.
Now is the judgment of this world. Now the ruler of this world is being thrown out.
And when I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw everyone to myself.”
He said this to show what kind of death he would die.
The crowds said to him, “We have heard from the Law that the Messiah remains forever. How can you say that the Son of Man is to be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”
Jesus said to them, “The light is with you for a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness does not overtake you. Whoever walks in darkness does not know where he is going.
While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become children of light.” Jesus said these things, then went away and hid from them.
Although he had performed all these signs before them, they did not believe in him.
So that the words of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, who said, “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”
For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah also said:
“They have blinded their eyes and darkened their hearts, so that they may not see with their eyes or understand with their hearts and turn back, and I would heal them.”
Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory and spoke about him.
Even among the leaders, many believed in him. But because of the Pharisees, they did not acknowledge it, so that they would not be excluded from the synagogue.
For they loved praise from people more than praise from God.
Jesus cried out, “Whoever believes in me believes not in me but in the one who sent me.
And whoever sees me sees the one who sent me.
I have come into the world as a light, so that everyone who believes in me may not remain in darkness.
If anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. For I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
Whoever rejects me and does not accept my words has someone who judges him. The word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day.
For I have not spoken on my own authority. Rather, the Father who sent me has himself given me a commandment about what to say and what to speak.
And I know that his commandment is eternal life. So whatever I say, I say just as my Father has told me.
Before the Passover festival, Jesus knew that the hour had come for him to leave this world and go to his Father. He loved his own who were in this world, and he loved them to the end.
While supper was taking place, Satan had already put it into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, to betray him.
Now Jesus, knowing that the Father had given everything into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going to God,
got up from supper, laid aside his clothes, took a linen towel, and tied it around his waist.
He poured water into a basin and began to wash his disciples' feet and wipe them with the linen towel tied around his waist.
When he came to Simon Peter, Simon said to him, “Lord, are you washing my feet?”
Jesus answered him, “You do not understand what I am doing now, but afterward you will understand.”
Simon Peter said to him, “You will never wash my feet.” Jesus said to him, “Unless I wash you, you have no share with me.”
Simon Peter said to him, “Then, Lord, wash not only my feet, but also my hands and my head.”
Jesus said to him, “Someone who has bathed needs only to wash his feet, for he is entirely clean. You too are all clean—but not all of you.”
For Jesus knew the one who would betray him. That is why he said, “Not all of you are clean.”
After he had washed their feet, he took his clothes and reclined at the table. He said to them, “Do you understand what I have done for you?”
“You call me ‘Our Teacher’ and ‘Our Lord,’ and you are right to say so, for that is what I am.
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, how much more ought you to wash one another's feet!
For I have given you this example, so that you too should do just as I have done for you.
Truly, truly, I tell you, no servant is greater than his master, and no messenger is greater than the one who sent him.
If you know these things, you are blessed if you do them.
I am not speaking about all of you, for I know those whom I have chosen. But this is so that the Scripture may be fulfilled: ‘The one who eats bread with me has raised his heel against me.’
I am telling you now, before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe that I am.
Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever receives anyone I send receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.”
After Jesus said these things, he was troubled in his spirit and testified, saying, “Truly, truly, I tell you, one of you will betray me.”
The disciples looked at one another, because they did not know whom he was speaking about.
One of his disciples, the one Jesus loved, was reclining against his chest.
Simon Peter motioned to this disciple to ask him who it was that he was speaking about.
That disciple leaned back against Jesus’ chest and said to him, “My Lord, who is it?”
Jesus answered, “It is the one to whom I give the bread after dipping it.” Then Jesus dipped the bread and gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot.
After the bread, Satan entered him. Jesus said to him, “What you are doing, do quickly.”
But none of those reclining at the table knew why he had said this to him.
Some thought that, because Judas had the money box, he had instructed him to buy something needed for the festival, or to give something to the poor.
Judas took the bread immediately and went outside. It was night when he went out.
Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in him.
If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and will glorify him immediately.
My children, I am with you only a little longer. You will look for me, and just as I told the Jews, ‘You cannot come where I am going,’ so I now tell you.
I give you a new commandment: love one another. Just as I have loved you, you too are to love one another.
By this everyone will know that you are my disciples: if you have love for one another.”
Simon Peter said to him, “Our Lord, where are you going?” Jesus answered him, “You cannot follow me now where I am going, but you will follow later.”
Simon Peter said to him, “My Lord, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.”
Jesus said to him, “Will you lay down your life for me? Truly, truly, I tell you, the rooster will not crow until you have denied me three times.
Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, and believe in me.
There are many dwelling places in my Father’s house. If it were not so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you.
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and take you to be with me, so that you too may be where I am.
You know where I am going, and you know the way.”
Thomas said to him, “Our Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?”
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to my Father except through me.”
If you knew me, you would also know my Father. From now on you know him and have seen him.
Philip said to him, “Our Lord, show us the Father, and that is enough for us.”
Jesus said to him, “I have been with you all this time, and you have not known me, Philip? Whoever sees me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?”
“Do you not believe that I am in my Father and my Father is in me? The words I speak, I do not speak on my own. Rather, my Father who dwells in me does these works.
Believe that I am in my Father and my Father is in me. Otherwise, believe at least because of the works.
Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do, and will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.
Whatever you ask in my name, I will do for you, so that the Father may be glorified in his Son.
If you ask me in my name, I will do it.
If you love me, keep my commandments.
And I will ask my Father, and he will give you another Advocate to be with you forever:
the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive because it neither sees him nor knows him. But you know him, because he lives with you and is in you.
I will not leave you as orphans, for I am coming to you. In a little while,
the world will not see me, but you will see me. Because I live, you too will live.
On that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you are in me, and I am in you.
Whoever has my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me. Whoever loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and reveal myself to him.
Judas—not Iscariot—said to him, “Lord, why are you going to reveal yourself to us and not to the world?”
Jesus answered him, “Whoever loves me keeps my word, and my Father will love him. We will come to him and make our home with him.
But whoever does not love me does not keep my word. This word that you hear is not mine, but belongs to the Father who sent me.
I have spoken these things to you while I am with you.
But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom my Father will send in my name, will teach you everything and remind you of everything I say to you.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled or afraid.
You heard me tell you, ‘I am going away, and I am coming to you.’ If you loved me, you would rejoice that I am going to my Father, because my Father is greater than I.
And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens, you will believe.
From now on I will not speak much with you, for the ruler of the world is coming, and he has no claim on me.
But so that the world may know that I love my Father, I do just as my Father commanded me. Get up; let us leave here.”
I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener.
Every branch in me that does not bear fruit he removes, and every branch that bears fruit he prunes so that it will bear much fruit.
You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.
Remain in me, and I in you. Just as a branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains on the vine, neither can you unless you remain in me.
I am the vine, and you are the branches. Whoever remains in me, and I in him, bears much fruit, because without me you can do nothing.
If anyone does not remain in me, he is thrown outside like a branch that dries up. They gather it and throw it into the fire to be burned.
But if you remain in me and my words remain in you, whatever you wish to ask for will be yours.
The Father is glorified in this: that you bear much fruit and become my disciples.
Just as my Father has loved me, I too have loved you. Remain in my love.
If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and remain in his love.
I have spoken these things to you so that my joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.
This is my commandment: love one another as I have loved you.
There is no greater love than this: that someone lay down his life for his friends.
You are my friends if you do everything I command you.
I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know what his master is doing. But I have called you my friends, because I have made known to you everything I heard from my Father.
You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you to go and bear fruit, and for your fruit to remain, so that my Father may give you whatever you ask him in my name.
I command you these things so that you may love one another.
And if the world hates you, know that it hated me before you.
If you belonged to the world, the world would love its own. But you do not belong to the world, for I chose you out of the world. That is why the world hates you.
Remember what I told you: no servant is greater than his master. If they persecuted me, they will persecute you too. And if they kept my word, they will keep yours too.
But they will do all these things to you because of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin. But now they have no excuse for their sin.
Whoever hates me also hates my Father.
And if I had not done works before their eyes that no one else had done, they would have no sin. But now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.
This is so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: ‘They hated me without cause.’
But when the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from my Father—the Spirit of truth, who comes forth from my Father—he will testify about me.
You also testify, because you have been with me from the beginning.
I have spoken these things to you so that you may not stumble.
For they will expel you from their synagogues. And the time will come when everyone who kills you will think he is offering a sacrifice to God.
They will do these things because they have known neither my Father nor me.
I have spoken these things to you so that when their time comes, you may remember them, that I told you about them. But I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.
But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’
For I have told you these things, and sorrow has come and filled your hearts.
But I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you.
And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment.
Concerning sin, because they do not believe in me.
Concerning righteousness, because I am going to my Father, and you will no longer see me.
Concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
I still have much to tell you, but you cannot take it in now.
But when the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth. For he will not speak from his own mind, but will speak whatever he hears, and he will make known to you the things to come.
And he will glorify me, because he will take what is mine and make it known to you.
Everything my Father has is mine. That is why I told you that he will take what is mine and make it known to you.
In a little while you will not see me, and again in a little while you will see me, because I am going to the Father.
His disciples were saying to one another, “What does he mean by saying to us, ‘In a little while you will not see me, and again in a little while you will see me,’ and, ‘I am going to my Father’?”
And they were saying, “What is this ‘little while’ he spoke of? We do not know what he is talking about.”

But Jesus knew that they wanted to question him, and he said to them, “Are you asking one another about this, because I told you, ‘In a little while you will not see me, and again in a little while you will see me’?
Truly, truly, I tell you, you will weep and mourn, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will turn into joy.

When a woman gives birth, she is in distress because the day for her delivery has come. But when she has given birth to a son, she no longer remembers her suffering, because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
You too are sorrowful now. But I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
And on that day you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly, I tell you, whatever you ask my Father in my name, he will give you.
Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.
I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. But the time is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures of speech, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
On that day you will ask in my name. And I am not telling you that I will ask the Father on your behalf,
for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.
I came from the Father and entered the world. Now I am leaving the world again and going to the Father.”
His disciples said to him, “Look, now you are speaking plainly and are not using a single figure of speech.”
Now we know that you know everything and do not need anyone to question you. Because of this, we believe that you came from God.
Jesus said to them, “Believe.”
For look, the time is coming, and has now come, when you will be scattered, each to his own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
I have told you these things so that in me you may have peace. In the world you have suffering. But take courage: I have overcome the world.
Jesus spoke these things, raised his eyes to heaven, and said, “My Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son, so that your Son may glorify you,
just as you have given him authority over all humanity, so that he may give eternal life to all whom you have given him.
And this is eternal life: that they know you, that you alone are the true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you sent.
I have glorified you on earth. I have completed the work you gave me to do.
And now, my Father, glorify me in your presence with the glory I had with you before the world existed.
I have made your name known to the people you gave me out of the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.
Now I know that everything you have given me comes from you.
For I have given them the words you gave me. They have received them and have truly known that I came from you, and they have believed that you sent me.
I pray for them. I do not pray for the world, but for those you have given me, because they are yours.
Everything that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine, and I am glorified in them.
I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, which you have given me, so that they may be one as we are.
While I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name. I guarded those you gave me, and none of them was lost except the son of destruction, so that Scripture might be fulfilled.
But now I am coming to you, and I say these things in the world so that my joy may be complete in them.
I have given them your word, and the world has hated them because they do not belong to the world, just as I do not belong to the world.
I do not ask you to take them out of the world, but to keep them from the evil one.
For they do not belong to the world, just as I do not belong to the world.
Father, make them holy through your truth, for your word is truth.
Just as you sent me into the world, I have also sent them into the world.
And for their sake I consecrate myself, so that they too may be made holy in truth.
I pray not only for these, but also for those who believe in me through their word,
so that they may all be one. Just as you, my Father, are in me and I am in you, may they too be one in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.
I have given them the glory you gave me, so that they may be one, just as we are one.
I am in them, and you are in me, so that they may be made perfectly one, and so that the world may know that you sent me and that you have loved them just as you have loved me.
Father, I want those you have given me to be with me where I am, so that they may see my glory, which you have given me, because you loved me before the foundations of the world.
My righteous Father, the world has not known you, but I have known you, and they have known that you sent me.
I have made your name known to them, and I am making it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I may be in them.
Jesus said these things and went out with his disciples across the Kidron Valley, where there was a garden, which he and his disciples entered.
Judas, the betrayer, also knew that place, because Jesus often gathered there with his disciples.
So Judas brought a company of soldiers, along with guards from the chief priests and Pharisees, and came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.
Jesus, knowing everything that was coming upon him, went out and said to them, “Who are you looking for?”
They said to him, “Jesus of Nazareth.” Jesus said to them, “I am he.” Judas, the betrayer, was also standing with them.
When Jesus said to them, “I am he,” they moved backward and fell to the ground.
Jesus asked them again, “Who are you looking for?” They said, “Jesus of Nazareth.”
Jesus said to them, “I told you that I am he. So if you are looking for me, let these people go.”
This was so that the words he had spoken would be fulfilled: “Of those you gave me, I have not lost even one.”
Simon Peter had a sword with him. He drew it, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.
Jesus said to Peter, “Put the sword into its sheath. Shall I not drink the cup my Father has given me?”
Then the military unit, the commanders, and the Jewish guards seized Jesus and bound him.
They brought him first to Annas, because he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
It was Caiaphas who had advised the Jews that it was better for one man to die on behalf of the people.
Simon Peter and one of the other disciples were following Jesus. The high priest knew that disciple, and he went into the courtyard with Jesus.
But Simon was standing outside by the gate. The other disciple, whom the high priest knew, went out, spoke to the woman keeping watch at the gate, and brought Simon inside.
