The young woman keeping watch at the gate said to Simon, “You are not also one of this man’s disciples, are you?” He said to her, “No.”
The servants and guards were standing there and had made a fire to warm themselves, because it was cold. Simon was also standing with them, warming himself.
The high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching.
Jesus said to him, “I have spoken openly to the people. I have always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I have said nothing in secret.
Why are you questioning me? Ask those who heard what I said to them. They know everything I said.”
When he said this, one of the guards standing there struck Jesus on the cheek and said to him, “Is that how you answer the high priest?”
Jesus answered him, “If I have spoken wrongly, testify to what was wrong. But if I have spoken rightly, why did you strike me?”
Then Annas sent Jesus, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said to him, “You are not also one of his disciples, are you?” He denied it and said, “I am not.”
One of the high priest’s servants, a relative of the man whose ear Simon had cut off, said to him, “Did I not see you with him in the garden?”
Simon denied it again, and at that very moment a rooster crowed.

Then they brought Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor’s headquarters. It was morning. They themselves did not enter the governor’s headquarters, so that they would not become ritually defiled before eating the Passover meal.
So Pilate went outside to them and said, “What accusation do you have against this man?”
They answered him, “If he were not doing evil things, we would not have handed him over to you.”
Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law.” The Jews said to him, “We are not permitted to put anyone to death.”
This was to fulfill what Jesus had said when he indicated what kind of death he was going to die.
Then Pilate entered the governor’s headquarters, called Jesus, and said to him, “Are you the king of the Jews?”
Jesus said to him, “Did you say this on your own, or did others tell you about me?”
Pilate said to him, “Am I a Jew? Your own people and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?”

Jesus said to him, “My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would have fought to keep me from being handed over to the Jews. But as it is, my kingdom is not from here.”

Pilate said to him, “So you are a king?” Jesus said to him, “You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to my voice.”
Pilate said to him, “What is truth?” After saying this, he went out again to the Jews and said to them, “I find no charge at all against him.”
“But you have a custom that I release someone for you at Passover. Do you therefore want me to release this king of the Jews for you?”
They all shouted, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now this Barabbas was a bandit.
Then Pilate had Jesus flogged.
The soldiers wove a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and they clothed him in purple garments.
They said, “Greetings, King of the Jews!” and struck him on his cheeks.
Pilate went outside again and said to them, “Look, I am bringing him out to you so that you may know that I find no charge at all against him.”
Jesus came outside wearing the crown of thorns and the purple clothes. Pilate said to them, “Here is the man!”
When the chief priests and the guards saw him, they shouted, “Crucify him! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no charge against him.”
The Jews said to him, “We have a law, and according to our law he deserves death, because he made himself the Son of God.”
When Pilate heard this statement, he became even more afraid.
He entered the governor’s headquarters again and said to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.
Pilate said to him, “Are you not speaking to me? Do you not know that I have authority to release you and authority to crucify you?”
Jesus said to him, “You would have no authority at all over me unless it had been given to you from above. For this reason, the one who handed me over to you has a greater sin than yours.”
Because of this, Pilate wanted to release him. But the Jews kept shouting, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. For everyone who makes himself a king is an opponent of Caesar.”
When Pilate heard this statement, he brought Jesus outside and sat down on the judgment seat, at the place called the Stone Pavement, which in Hebrew is called Gabbatha.
It was the Friday of Passover, about the sixth hour. He said to the Jews, “Here is your king!”
But they shouted, “Take him away! Take him away! Crucify him! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your king?” The chief priests said, “We have no king except Caesar.”
Then he handed him over to them to be crucified. They took Jesus and led him out,
carrying his cross, to the place called the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
There they crucified him, and with him two others, one on either side, with Jesus in the middle.
Pilate also wrote a notice and placed it on his cross. It read: “This is Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the Jews.”
Many of the Jews read this notice, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city. It was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.
The chief priests said to Pilate, “Do not write that he is the King of the Jews, but that he said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’”
Pilate said, “What I have written, I have written.”
When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they took his clothes and divided them into four shares, one share for each soldier. His tunic, however, was seamless, woven in one piece from the top.

They said to one another, “Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it to see whose it will be.” And the scripture was fulfilled that says, “They divided my clothes among themselves, and cast lots for my clothing.” This is what the soldiers did.
Standing near the cross of Jesus were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing there, and he said to his mother, “Woman, here is your son.”
And he said to that disciple, “Here is your mother.” From that hour, that disciple took her into his home.
After this, Jesus knew that everything had been completed, and, so that the scripture would be fulfilled, he said, “I am thirsty.”
A container full of sour wine was standing there. They filled a sponge with the sour wine, put it on hyssop, and brought it to his mouth.
When Jesus had taken the sour wine, he said, “It is now finished.” He bowed his head and gave up his spirit.

Because it was Friday, the Jews said, “These bodies must not remain overnight on their crosses, because the Sabbath is approaching.” For that Sabbath was a great day. They asked Pilate to have the legs of those who were crucified broken and to have them taken down.
The soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man and of the other man who had been crucified with him.
When they came to Jesus, they saw that he was already dead, and they did not break his legs.
Instead, one of the soldiers struck him in the side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
The one who saw it has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he has spoken the truth, so that you too may believe.
These things happened so that the scripture would be fulfilled that says, “Not one of his bones will be broken.”
And again, another scripture says, “They will look at the one they pierced.”

After these things, Joseph of Arimathea asked Pilate for permission to take away Jesus’ body. He was a disciple of Jesus, but kept it secret for fear of the Jews. Pilate gave permission, so he came and took Jesus’ body away.
Nicodemus also came—the one who had previously come to Jesus at night—and brought with him a mixture of myrrh and aloes, weighing about a hundred pounds.
They took Jesus’ body and wrapped it in linen cloths with spices, according to the Jewish burial custom.
Now there was a garden at the place where Jesus was crucified, and in the garden was a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
They laid Jesus there because the Sabbath was approaching and because the tomb was nearby.
On the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb early in the morning, while it was still dark, and saw that the stone had been taken away from the tomb.
She ran to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and said to them, “They have taken our Lord away from the tomb, and I do not know where they have laid him.”
Simon and the other disciple went out and headed for the tomb.
Both were running together, but the other disciple ran ahead of Simon and reached the tomb first.
He peered in and saw the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go inside.
Simon came after him, entered the tomb, and saw the linen cloths lying there.
The cloth that had been tied around his head was not with the linen cloths, but was rolled up and laid aside in a place by itself.
Then the disciple who had reached the tomb first also went in. He saw and believed.
For they did not yet understand from the Scriptures that he was to rise from the dead.
Then the disciples went back to their own place.
But Mary stood by the tomb, weeping. As she wept, she peered into the tomb
and saw two angels in white sitting where Jesus’ body had been laid, one at the head and one at the feet.
They said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She said to them, “They have taken my Lord away, and I do not know where they have laid him.”
After saying this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, but she did not know that it was Jesus.

Jesus said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for?” She thought he was the gardener and said to him, “Sir, if you have taken him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will go and take him away.”
Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and said to him in Hebrew, “Rabbuli,” which means “Teacher.”
Jesus said to her, “Do not come near me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brothers and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and to my God and your God.’”
Then Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples the good news that she had seen our Lord and that he had said these things to her.

When evening came on that day, the first day of the week, the doors where the disciples were staying were shut for fear of the Jews. Jesus came and stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.”
After saying this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples rejoiced when they saw our Lord.
Jesus said to them again, “Peace be with you. Just as my Father sent me, I also am sending you.”
After saying these things, he breathed on them and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit.”
If you forgive anyone's sins, they will be forgiven him. And if you retain anyone's sins, they are retained.
But Thomas, one of the Twelve, who was called the Twin, was not there with them when Jesus came.
The disciples told him, “We have seen our Lord.” But he said to them, “Unless I see the nail marks in his hands, put my fingers into them, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.”
Eight days later, the disciples were inside again, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came while the doors were shut, stood among them, and said to them, “Peace be with you.”
He said to Thomas, “Bring your finger here and look at my hands. Bring your hand and put it into my side. Do not be unbelieving, but believing.”
Thomas answered and said to him, “My Lord and my God!”
Jesus said to him, “Now that you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen me and have believed.”
Jesus also did many other signs before his disciples that are not written in this book.
But these have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and that when you believe, you may have eternal life in his name.
After these things, Jesus showed himself again to his disciples by the Sea of Tiberias. He showed himself in this way:
Simon Peter, Thomas who was called the Twin, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples were together.
Simon Peter said to them, “I am going fishing.” They said to him, “We are coming with you too.” They went out and got into the boat, but that night they caught nothing.
When morning came, Jesus stood beside the sea, but the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.
Jesus said to them, “Children, do you have anything to eat?” They said to him, “No.”
He said to them, “Cast your net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” They cast it, and they could not haul the net in because of the great number of fish it had caught.

The disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is our Lord!” When Simon heard that it was our Lord, he took his tunic and tied it around his waist, because he was naked. He threw himself into the sea to come to Jesus.
The other disciples came in the boat, for they were not far from land, only about two hundred cubits away. They were dragging the net full of fish.
When they came ashore, they saw a charcoal fire laid there, with fish lying on it, and bread.
Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish you have just caught.”
Simon Peter went up and hauled the net ashore, full of large fish, one hundred and fifty-three of them. Despite all that weight, the net did not tear.
Jesus said to them, “Come and eat.” None of the disciples dared to ask him who he was, because they knew that it was our Lord.
Jesus came forward, took the bread and fish, and gave them to them.
This was the third time Jesus appeared to his disciples after he rose from the dead.

When they had finished eating, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord. You know that I love you.” He said to him, “Feed my lambs.”
He said to him again, a second time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord. You know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Tend my sheep.”

He said to him a third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?” Peter was grieved because he had asked him a third time, “Do you love me?” He said to him, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Tend my ewes.”

“Truly, truly, I tell you, when you were young, you used to fasten your own belt and walk wherever you wanted. But when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will fasten your belt and take you where you do not want to go.”
He said this to show by what kind of death he would glorify God. After saying these things, he said to him, “Follow me.”
Simon Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following him—the one who had leaned against Jesus’ chest at supper and said, “Lord, who is going to betray you?”
When Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?”
Jesus said to him, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”

So this saying spread among the brothers: that this disciple would not die. But Jesus had not said that he would not die. Rather, he had said, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?”
This is the disciple who testified about all these things and also wrote them down. We know that his testimony is true.
There are also many other things that Jesus did. If they were written down one by one, I think that even the world itself would not have room for the books that would be written.
